sec: Testing algorithm and opportunistic infections by CD4 count

items.q: Which assay does the page print as currently in use for HIV testing?
items.exp: 'Currently in use : 4th generation combined antigen antibody assay : HIV-1/HIV-2 antigen/antibody combination immunoassay'. (Book p1066)

items.q: Algorithm — match the result to the next step — 1) Negative 2) Positive … A) HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay B) No HIV
items.exp: 'Interpretation : · If negative : No HIV. · If positive : HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay'. (Book p1066)

items.q: Differentiation assay outcomes — match — 1) HIV-1 antibodies detected 2) HIV-2 antibodies detected 3) No antibodies detected … A) HIV-2 infection B) HIV-1 NAT needed C) HIV-1 infection
items.exp: 'HIV-1 antibodies detected', 'HIV-2 antibodies detected' and 'No HIV antibodies detected → HIV-1 NAT'. (Book p1066)

items.q: HIV-1 NAT — match — 1) Positive 2) Negative … A) Negative for HIV-1 B) Acute HIV-1 infection
items.exp: 'HIV-1 NAT : Positive → Acute HIV-1 infection; Negative → Negative for HIV-1'. (Book p1066)

items.q: A 4th-generation assay is positive but the HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation immunoassay detects no antibodies. What is the printed next step and its interpretation?
opts: HIV-1 NAT — positive means acute HIV-1 infection
Start antiretroviral therapy immediately without further tests
Report the patient as HIV negative
items.exp: 'No HIV antibodies detected → HIV-1 NAT → Positive : Acute HIV-1 infection; Negative : Negative for HIV-1'. (Book p1066)

items.q: Opportunistic infections by CD4 — match — 1) Around 600 2) Around 300 3) Around 200 … A) Oral hairy leukoplakia or TB, mucocutaneous herpes, cryptosporidiosis, microsporidiosis B) Pneumocystis jirovecii, miliary TB, oesophageal candidiasis C) Lymphadenopathy and thrombocytopenia
items.exp: The CD4-stratified table lists lymphadenopathy/thrombocytopenia near 600, mucocutaneous herpes and the diarrhoeal parasites around 300, and Pneumocystis, miliary TB and oesophageal candidiasis around 200. (Book p1066)

items.q: At what CD4 level is Kaposi's sarcoma printed as occurring?
Low CD4 infections — match — 1) Cerebral toxoplasmosis 2) Cryptococcal meningitis 3) Primary CNS lymphoma … A) CD4 around 100 B) CD4 around 100 C) CD4 50 – 100
items.exp: The table places cerebral toxoplasmosis and cryptococcal meningitis around a CD4 count of 100, with primary CNS lymphoma at 50-100. (Book p1066)

items.q: Very low CD4 conditions — match — 1) HIV-associated dementia 2) PML 3) CMV retinitis 4) Mycobacterium avium intracellulare … A) Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy B) Cytomegalovirus retinitis C) Disseminated MAC disease D) HIV-associated dementia
items.exp: All four are printed at the lowest CD4 stratum of the opportunistic-infection table. (Book p1066)

items.q: Which is NOT printed in the CD4-stratified opportunistic-infection table?
items.exp: The table lists lymphadenopathy/thrombocytopenia, Kaposi's sarcoma, oral hairy leukoplakia and TB, mucocutaneous herpes, cryptosporidiosis, microsporidiosis, Pneumocystis, miliary TB, oesophageal candidiasis, cerebral toxoplasmosis, cryptococcal meningitis, primary CNS lymphoma, HIV-associated dementia, PML, CMV retinitis and MAC disease. (Book p1066)
